To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in situ hybridization histochemical (ISHH) techniques can be used to identify neurons which express mRNAs encoding glutamine synthetase (GS) and the enzymes involved in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter glutamate (glutamic acid decaroxylase, glutaminase and aspartate amineransferase) in rat brain.

the distribution of mRNAs encoding GluT, AspT and GAD is consistent with previous immunocytochemical studies, and that the distribution of GluT and GAD mRNA in the brain is consistent with the distribution of glutamaterg and GABAergic neurons.
the distribution of GABAergic neurons in the brain, as defined by GAD mRNA, is similar to that seen with antibodies to GAD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new techniques for the study of brain chemistry.
the distribution of glutamate, aspartate and GABA in the rat brain and spinal cord.
the distribution of glutaminase, AspT and GAD in rat brain, and the relationship of their distribution with other enzymes of the GABAergic pathway, such as GAD and glutamine synthetase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GAD is a marker for GABAergic neurons; that AspT is a marker for a subset of neurons that may use GABA or glutamate as neurotransmitters; and that GluT is a marker of glutamatergig neurons, although it is not clear whether all neurons containing GluT mRNA are glutamatergics.

the GAD and GluT mRNA are present in different neuronal populations, and the AspT mRNA is present in a different set of neurons, some of which may be glutameric, some may be GABAergic and some may be neither.
GluT mRNA appears to be present in all neurons using glutamate as a transmitter, AspT mRNA is present in many, but not all, of those same neurons, and GAD mRNA is present in a subset of those cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of GluT, AspT and GAD mRNA is consistent with the known distribution of glutamatergics and GABAergic neuronal systems in the brain.
GAD mRNA is present in the GABAergic neurons and the GluT is present in the excitatory neurons.
GAD is a marker for GABAergic neurons and AspT for neurons that are GABAergic or that are GABA-ergic/glutamatergic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of GAD as a marker for GABA neurons is a bit of a misnomer.
the GABAergic neurons of the striatum, globus pallidus, and substantia nigra do not express GAD mRNA.

the GAD mRNA is widely distributed, and that the GluT and AspT mRNAs are not confined to neurons that use GABA and glutamate, respectively, but are also expressed in a variety of neurons that do not contain significant amounts of either of these neurotransmitters.
